# dead-code-pruner

> Conservative multi-language dead-code elimination for feature-flag cleanup, boolean constant folding, and static-analysis-driven source cleanup.

dead-code-pruner uses tree-sitter to replace permanently true/false feature flags with literals, simplify boolean expressions, eliminate dead if-branches, inline constant-return methods, and remove safe dead method definitions in a 3-phase iterative pipeline until convergence. It targets dead code cleanup for Java, Kotlin, Android, Swift, iOS, TypeScript, JavaScript, Go, Rust, C, C++, and C# projects while preserving dynamic framework entry points.

## Documentation

- [README](https://github.com/OldJii/dead-code-pruner/blob/main/README.md): Pipeline, configuration, architecture, and usage
- [pruner.example.yaml](https://github.com/OldJii/dead-code-pruner/blob/main/pruner.example.yaml): Example config

## Pipeline

**Phase 1** — Constant folding + boolean simplification (steps 1–4, loops until stable)
**Phase 2** — Constant-return method inlining + cascade simplification
**Phase 3** — Dead method cleanup + cascade simplification

## Quick start

```bash
pip install -r requirements.txt
cp pruner.example.yaml pruner.yaml
python3 -m pruner /path/to/project --dry-run
python3 -m pruner /path/to/project
```

## Key facts

- **Languages**: Java, Kotlin, Go, C, C++, JS, TS, Rust, Swift, C# (extensible via tree-sitter)
- **Engine**: tree-sitter AST
- **Dependencies**: Python 3.10+, tree-sitter grammars, PyYAML
- **Safety**: annotation-aware, chain-call aware, inheritance-aware, comment/string safe
- **License**: MIT
